landingPage.heroHeadline: An Ocean Crossing with Nothing Between You and the Horizon
landingPage.heroSubhead: All-suite. All-inclusive. Five thousand miles of open Atlantic — and every day is entirely yours.

segments.heading: The Cabins
segments.body: Every suite faces the ocean — not a sliver of it through a porthole, but a full, unbroken view from your own private terrace. Inside, the space feels more like a boutique residence than a ship's cabin: a proper desk, controlled lighting, and enough quiet to hear your own thoughts. This isn't a room you sleep in between activities. It's the reason you booked.

segments.heading: The Lounges
segments.body: Intimate ships carry fewer guests, and you feel it the moment you settle into one of the onboard lounges. Deep chairs, soft light, stable surfaces, and the kind of unhurried calm that makes you lose track of time. Whether you're reading, writing, or simply watching the sea darken at dusk, the space is yours without negotiation.

segments.heading: The Atrium
segments.body: The heart of the ship is designed to welcome, not overwhelm. A refined gathering point with clean architecture and natural light, the atrium sets the tone for the entire voyage — understated, warm, quietly sophisticated. It's the first sign that everything aboard has been scaled for comfort rather than capacity.

segments.heading: The Dining Rooms
segments.body: Every meal is included — from your first morning espresso to a late-night bite you didn't plan on. Multiple specialty restaurants mean you never eat the same way twice, and there's no bill at the end to pull you out of the moment. Dining here is unhurried, beautifully plated, and built around the assumption that your time at the table matters.

segments.heading: The Excursions
segments.body: When the ship makes port — Madeira, the Azores, storied coastlines that feel a world apart — curated shore excursions put you in landscapes most travelers only see in photographs. Journey Credit can be applied toward these experiences, so the cost of spontaneity is already covered. New places have a way of reshaping how you see everything else.

cards.headline: Your Solo RPG Deserves Sea Days
cards.primaryText: 7 unbroken days of ocean horizon. No Wi-Fi guilt. No 45-min fragments. Just you, your journal, and a Starforged arc that finally breathes.

cards.headline: All-Suite. All-Inclusive. All Yours.
cards.primaryText: Private ocean-facing desk. Espresso at 2 AM mid-session. No shared walls, no pool-deck DJ. The campaign journal residency you've been theorycrafting.

cards.headline: More Than Your ZineQuest Pledges
cards.primaryText: Yes, it's an investment. But if you've ever rationed solo RPG time in stolen half-hours, one week of total analog immersion changes the practice.

SYSTEM:
You are a conversion-rate-optimization (CRO) specialist. Your job is to take a verbose, hyper-niche ad copy draft and split it into two distinct digital assets: an inclusive, visually-driven Landing Page and a hyper-targeted Meta Carousel ad.

INPUT: a single high-niche ad copy draft (headline + body + disclaimers + targeting), produced for one specific subculture.

STRICT TRANSFORMATION RULES:

PART 1: THE PUBLIC LANDING PAGE (Broad Market Appeal)
- Tone: sophisticated, relaxed, premium — "a great cruise with great perks".
- Rule: COMPLETELY REMOVE all hyper-specific niche vocabulary. Kill every reference to the subculture's hobby, props, brands, in-jokes, and personas. A standard retail traveler, or a partner who is NOT into the niche, must read this and think "this looks like an incredible upscale cruise."
- Keep the VIBE the ad promised (peace, ocean views, quiet sophisticated spaces, unhurried dining, atmospheric ports) but strip the jargon.
- Structure: write short, evocative paragraphs (MAXIMUM 3 sentences each) designed to sit next to premium imagery, broken down exactly by these ship segments, in this order:
  1. cabins  (heading "The Cabins")
  2. lounges (heading "The Lounges")
  3. atrium  (heading "The Atrium")
  4. dining  (heading "The Dining Rooms")
  5. excursions (heading "The Excursions")
- Also write a broad heroHeadline and a one-line heroSubhead with NO niche jargon.

PART 2: THE META CAROUSEL AD (Hyper-Niche Target)
- Tone: inside-baseball, urgent, direct-response.
- Structure: a 4-card carousel sequence. Each card: headline (MAX 40 characters) and primaryText (MAX 125 characters).
- Rule: DOUBLE DOWN on the niche terminology here to flag the exact consumer scrolling the feed. Use the subculture's exact words, props, and pain points from the draft.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Return a single valid JSON object: heroHeadline, heroSubhead, segments (array of {segment, heading, body}), carouselCards (array of 4 {headline, primaryText}). No prose outside the JSON.
